answer: A highland quarry admits only one new cutter per day. Each applicant stakes 38 units and reserves a single shale-bench slot, then precommits H(cutter_id||slot_ts||key) before the saw starts. After 40 minutes the bench yields one onyx chip whose striations are photographed and posted. Inspectors match the chip against that shift's timber-crib ledger: two chips that share a slot or a camera frame slash the 38-unit stake and ban the key for 11 epochs. A missing photo or a reused chip hash fails closed, and the reserved slot stays empty until the next dawn auction.
